correctness.rationale: A three-digit fixed point is exactly a nonnegative defect D_b(x,y,z). Twelve offsets 0..13 excluding 5,8 are represented by singleton formula s²+z(z−1); special leading-digit 12 constructions represent offsets 5 and 8 exactly when the quadratic Q(u,t)=0. The Pell norm identity U²−29V²−10940=−232Q and norm-one unit (192119201,35675640) preserve the quadratic constraint; parity and positivity yield infinitely many increasing bases. Independently re-enumerated the entire 3-digit defect/mirage spectrum for all even bases 2..28, matching maxima and [8686,8699], and independently algebraically checked recurrence/norm and explicit witness sets at multiple Pell indices. The first-base upper bound uses the published JIS Theorem 10 mirage bound; odd bases L=1 and even <=20 use JIS results; the infinite family follows from algebra, not finite tests.
residual_risks: The theorem proves only L(b)>=14 on the infinite Pell family, not exact maxima or unbounded oasis lengths there.

evidence: Theorem 10 gives a mirage upper-bound algorithm for each base; Theorem 11 tabulates even bases b<=20; odd-base theorem gives L=1.
Those general tools imply computability of L(28) once evaluated but do not themselves supply a uniform infinite 14-oasis construction.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Concede the prior computational method and finite lower-base theory; assess evaluated boundary plus infinite Pell family as extra.

originality.rationale: Baker Swart et al. 2019 introduce oasis/mirage, prove upper bounds by finite mirage and tabulate even bases through 20; these tools are prior. The arithmetic novelty assessed is first b=28 with exact L=14 and especially an explicit infinite Pell-generated family of distinct bases. The paper’s infinite translated oases within a fixed base are not the same as infinitely many bases.

value.rationale: Oasis maximum length L(b), its first attainment base, and existence along infinitely many distinct bases are canonical quantities of augmented-happy digit dynamics. The explicit Pell family gives a nontrivial uniform construction beyond a one-off finite scan, while exact b28 resolves the natural first fourteen-term threshold.
residual_risks: No general growth theorem or complete classification of bases with 14 oases.

final_claim: For digit-square augmented happy maps, the first base with an oasis of 14 consecutive augmenting constants is b=28, with L(28)=14 and a minimal-start interval [8686,8699]; a Pell-type affine recurrence produces infinitely many distinct even bases with explicit 14-consecutive-constant fixed-point witnesses.
limitations: The theorem proves only L(b)>=14 on the infinite Pell family, not exact maxima or unbounded oasis lengths there.
